mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the compressibility of gases?

options.A: Gases can be easily squeezed into a smaller volume
options.B: Gases have a fixed shape that cannot change
options.C: Gases always occupy the same volume regardless of pressure
options.D: Gases flow like liquids but cannot be compressed

mcqs.answer: Gases can be easily squeezed into a smaller volume
mcqs.explanation: Gases consist of particles far apart, so applying pressure reduces their volume; this property is called compressibility. Option A correctly defines it. The other options describe incorrect or unrelated properties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of a gas at room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Ice is solid water, not a gas. Oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapor are all gases at room temperature. Hence option D is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: What does it mean when we say a gas has "no fixed shape"?

options.A: It takes the shape of the container it is in
options.B: It keeps the shape it had when first placed
options.C: It has a permanent shape like a solid
options.D: It changes shape only when heated

mcqs.answer: It takes the shape of the container it is in
mcqs.explanation: Gases have no fixed shape; they spread out to fill the shape of any container they occupy. Option A captures this idea, while the other options describe properties of solids or incorrect behavior.

mcqs.question: If a gas is transferred from a small bottle into a larger empty container, what will happen to its volume?

options.A: The volume will stay the same as in the bottle
options.B: The gas will expand to fill the larger container

mcqs.answer: The gas will expand to fill the larger container
mcqs.explanation: Gases have no fixed volume; they expand to occupy all available space. Therefore the gas will spread out to fill the larger container. The other options contradict this fundamental property.

mcqs.question: When a balloon is released inside a room, the air from the balloon spreads out until it:

options.A: Remains confined to the balloon's original size

mcqs.explanation: This demonstrates the gas property of filling any available space. The released air expands and occupies the whole room, unlike the other options which are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: A gas escaping from a punctured tire spreads out and moves away from the hole. Which property of gases does this illustrate?
mcqs.explanation: Gases, like liquids, can flow from regions of higher pressure to lower pressure. The spreading of gas from the tire shows its ability to flow. The other options describe properties that gases do not possess.

mcqs.question: Identify the false statement about gases.

options.A: Gases can be compressed into a smaller volume
options.C: Gases fill any container they are placed in

mcqs.explanation: Gases do not have a fixed volume; they expand or compress depending on pressure. Option D is therefore false. Options A, B, and C correctly describe gas properties.

mcqs.question: Which of the following substances is a gas at ordinary room temperature?
mcqs.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere and is a gas at room temperature. Water in liquid form, iron, and sand are all solids or liquids under normal conditions, so they are not gases.
